definition: A reaction that releases energy to the surroundings, causing the temperature of the surroundings to increase.
clues: This is a type of chemical reaction
It releases energy to the surroundings
The temperature of the surroundings increases
A reaction that gives out heat — combustion, neutralisation and respiration are examples; temperature of surroundings rises

definition: A reaction that takes in energy from the surroundings, causing the temperature of the surroundings to decrease.
clues: This is a type of chemical reaction
It takes in energy from the surroundings
The temperature of the surroundings decreases
A reaction that absorbs heat — thermal decomposition and photosynthesis are examples; temperature of surroundings falls

definition: The minimum energy required for a reaction to occur — the energy needed to break existing bonds and start the reaction.
clues: This is a concept in reaction energetics
It is the minimum energy needed to start a reaction
Catalysts lower this value
The minimum energy reactant particles must have to react — shown on an energy profile diagram as the peak

definition: A diagram showing the relative energy levels of reactants and products in a reaction, and the activation energy needed.
clues: This is a type of diagram in chemistry
It shows the energy of reactants and products
It includes the activation energy as a peak
A diagram plotting energy against reaction progress — the peak represents the activation energy, the difference shows if the reaction is exo- or endothermic

definition: The energy required to break one mole of a particular type of bond (in kJ/mol). Breaking bonds requires energy; making bonds releases energy.
clues: This is a value associated with chemical bonds
Energy is needed to break a bond
Energy is released when a bond forms
The energy needed to break one mole of a specific bond — used to calculate the overall energy change of a reaction

definition: The process of breaking chemical bonds in reactants. This is endothermic — it requires energy from the surroundings.
clues: This is a process that occurs at the start of a reaction
It requires an input of energy
It is endothermic
Rupturing chemical bonds in reactants requires energy input — it is always an endothermic process

definition: The process of making new chemical bonds in products. This is exothermic — it releases energy to the surroundings.
clues: This is a process that occurs during a reaction
It releases energy to the surroundings
It is exothermic
Forming new bonds in the products releases energy — it is always an exothermic process

definition: The net energy transferred in a reaction. Calculated as: energy in (bond breaking) – energy out (bond forming). Negative = exothermic; positive = endothermic.
clues: This is a calculated value for a reaction
It depends on the difference between bond breaking and bond making energies
A negative value means the reaction is exothermic
Energy needed to break bonds minus energy released forming bonds — negative result means exothermic

definition: A device that reacts hydrogen and oxygen to produce electricity, with water as the only waste product.
clues: This is a device that generates electricity
It uses hydrogen as a fuel
The only waste product is water
An electrochemical cell that combines hydrogen and oxygen to generate electricity — water is the only product

definition: An electrochemical cell that continuously converts the chemical energy of a fuel into electrical energy, as long as fuel is supplied.
clues: This is a type of electrochemical device
It converts chemical energy into electrical energy
It works as long as fuel is continuously supplied
A device that continuously generates electricity from a fuel — unlike a battery, it does not run down as long as fuel is added

definition: An exothermic reaction between a fuel and oxygen that releases heat and light. Complete combustion produces CO₂ and H₂O.
clues: This is a type of chemical reaction
It is exothermic and requires oxygen
Complete versions produce CO₂ and water
Burning a fuel in oxygen — complete combustion produces carbon dioxide and water and releases large amounts of heat

definition: A technique used to measure the heat energy released or absorbed during a chemical reaction, typically by measuring temperature change in water.
clues: This is an experimental technique
It measures temperature change to calculate energy
It is used to compare fuels
A method of measuring energy changes in reactions by observing the temperature rise of a known mass of water

definition: The energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1°C. For water it is 4200 J/kg°C.
clues: This is a property of a substance
It is measured in J/kg°C
For water it is 4200 J/kg°C
The energy needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C — used in the equation Q = mcΔT to calculate energy released by fuels

definition: A reaction that can proceed in both directions. Products can react to reform the reactants, shown by the ⇌ symbol.
clues: This is a type of chemical reaction
It can go in both directions
It is shown by a double-headed arrow
A reaction that goes both forwards and backwards — shown as ⇌ — the system can reach a state of equilibrium

definition: The heat energy transferred during a reaction at constant pressure. Symbol: ΔH. Negative for exothermic, positive for endothermic.
clues: This is a measure of heat energy change in a reaction
Its symbol is ΔH
A negative value indicates an exothermic reaction
The heat transferred at constant pressure — ΔH is negative for exothermic reactions and positive for endothermic ones

definition: Energy stored in chemical bonds. Released or absorbed during chemical reactions when bonds are broken and formed.
clues: This is a type of stored energy
It is found in chemical bonds
It is released or absorbed during reactions
Energy stored in the bonds of compounds — released in exothermic reactions like combustion or stored in endothermic reactions

definition: In the context of fuel cells and combustion, oxidation is the reaction of a fuel with oxygen, releasing chemical energy.
clues: This is a process relevant to both combustion and fuel cells
It involves the reaction of a fuel with oxygen
It releases chemical energy
The reaction of hydrogen (or a hydrocarbon) with oxygen — the basis of both combustion and hydrogen fuel cells
